data.source_title: Hospital discharge and community support guidance
data.locator: Sections 5-6 (structure, roles, best practice); Annex A (operational discharge-to-assess process); Annex B (pathways 0-3); Annex C (discharge-process responsibilities).
data.source_setting: Official England NHS/local-authority hospital discharge guidance; describes acute/community hospitals and integrated care pathways.
data.source_period: Official guidance, accessed 2026-10-10; guidance applies in England.
data.source_n: Not applicable; official operating guidance, not an outcome study.
data.quantity: Documented discharge-planning and placement transition stages
value: start discharge planning at or before admission
identify current support and post-discharge needs with patient/family
coordinate health and social care through a multidisciplinary team/care transfer hub
select pathway: usual home, home with support, bed-based intermediate rehabilitation, or new residential/nursing placement
check service/bed availability and coordinate transfer
include social-work, safeguarding, advocacy, and carer needs where relevant
data.source_evidence_basis: The official guidance specifies four discharge-to-assess pathways and assigns coordination roles across hospital, health, social care, community providers, and care-transfer hubs; it directs early planning, needs assessment, and vacancy checks.
data.limitations: Policy guidance for England, not an observed hospital execution-time study and not US/RWJ policy. Local law, terminology, pathway design, staffing, eligibility and service capacity differ.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent discharge readiness, destination selection, referral, acceptance/authorization, transport, and post-discharge support as explicit linked states. Treat pathway choices and roles as candidate process structure requiring local workflow confirmation.
